<main class="site-main project-detail" id="content"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Experiment · Model inspection</p><h1>Neural Observatory</h1><p class="project-lede">Follow one recorded token through Gemma 3’s full architecture, then zoom into every measured MLP unit in a selected layer.</p><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">Recorded model responses</span><span>Gemma 3 · 1B parameters</span></div></section>

<iframe class="neuron-playground-frame" src="/assets/neuron-playground/index.html" title="Neural Observatory: explore recorded Gemma responses across all layers" loading="eager"></iframe>

<article class="prose"><h2>Begin with the architecture</h2><p>The explorer starts with the input token, embedding, 26 transformer blocks, and output. The blue bar in each block is the mean absolute z-score of its strongest 69 MLP units for the selected word. Orange diamonds mark global self-attention layers; they are not activation values.</p><p>Select a block to open its self-attention path, measured gated MLP stage, residual stream, and 96 × 72 unit field. Start with L12/U646, the first frozen winner, then use the word search to compare all 320 recorded words.</p><h2>What is measured</h2><p>These are saved target-token activations from a pretrained Gemma model. The controls choose which measurement to display. They do not run a new prompt, disable a unit, or change the model’s answer. A category mean is a descriptive response profile, not a probability, accuracy, or causal effect.</p><p><a class="button-link" href="/posts/looking-for-an-animal-neuron/">Read the experiment</a> <a class="text-link" href="/assets/neuron-playground/index.html">Open observatory on its own</a> <a class="text-link" href="/assets/neuron-playground/manifest.json">Download manifest</a></p></article>
